sources.title: Marine Le Pen: current constituency, profession and birthday
sources.findings: Read current Assembly profile: born August 5, 1968 in Neuilly-sur-Seine, lawyer, current RN deputy for Pas-de-Calais constituency 11. Current membership does not imply continued group presidency; the October replacement notice supersedes stale summaries. No contact details or personal correspondence used.

sources.title: Marine Le Pen: parliamentary terms beginning in 2017, 2022 and 2024
sources.findings: Read Sycomore mandates: June 21, 2017–June 21, 2022; June 22, 2022–June 9, 2024; current term from July 1, 2024. Formal mandate starts are distinct from election days. Do not claim an uninterrupted mandate through dissolution or confuse presidential and legislative elections.

sources.title: 2015 candidate biography: legal education, early mandates and 2012 election
sources.findings: Read Institut Montaigne’s 2015 biography: Paris II maîtrise 1990, criminal-law DEA 1991, CAPA 1992; first regional mandate 1998, January 2011 party congress, third place in 2012. Diploma nomenclature preserved rather than converting DEA into a PhD. Its municipal chronology is not relied on; omit unsupported exact dates from conflicting summaries.

sources.title: 2022 candidate biography: legal career, European elections and party renaming
sources.findings: Read Institut Montaigne’s 2022 candidate biography: Paris legal practice, 1998 move to party legal service, 2004/2009/2014 European elections, national deputy from 2017 and 2018 party renaming. Its July 2021 stepping-back shorthand is distinguished from Bardella’s September interim start and November 2022 permanent election. Stale candidate/current-role labels are not carried into 2026.

sources.title: Marine Le Pen succeeds Jean-Marie Le Pen as party president, 16 January 2011
sources.findings: Read contemporary Le Parisien January 16, 2011 report, not merely the title. Official result at Tours: succession to Jean-Marie Le Pen after defeating Bruno Gollnisch. Earlier leaks and later publication in another newspaper are not the formal succession date. No need to reproduce family details or assign her father’s legal record to her.

sources.title: Bardella elected RN president on 5 November 2022 after interim leadership
sources.findings: Read RTL November 5, 2022 report: Bardella elected permanent president, interim presidency since September 13, 2021; party formerly FN, renamed RN in 2018. Interim party management, permanent party presidency and Assembly group leadership are three distinct roles.

sources.title: Official final national results of the 2017 presidential election
sources.findings: Read Interior Ministry’s final national 2017 election table: May 7 runoff, Le Pen 10638475 votes and 33.90% of valid votes, Macron winner. The table separately lists registered-elector percentages and first-round figures; those denominators and rounds are not mixed.

sources.title: Official final national results of the 2022 presidential election
sources.findings: Read Interior Ministry’s final national 2022 table: April 24 runoff, Le Pen 13288686 votes and 41.45% of valid votes, Macron winner. Do not substitute early estimates, percentage of registered voters, first-round share or legislative seat totals.

sources.title: 30 June 2024 first-round legislative results, reported 1 July
sources.findings: Read Public Sénat’s July 1, 2024 roundup of the June 30 first round. Le Pen won constituency 11 with 32681 votes and 58.04%. Publication after midnight is not the election date; official Sycomore establishes July 1 mandate start. No full constituency ballot recount performed.

sources.title: Appeal conviction and Le Pen’s presidential announcement, 7 July 2026
sources.findings: Read Reuters’s July 7, 2026 completed-judgment and interview report via Investing.com. Conviction upheld, reduced electoral penalty, candidacy announcement and denial are separate facts. Later legal debate qualifies the initial report’s apparent certainty about eligibility; announcing cassation is not a final acquittal.

sources.title: Judicial situation: sentences, cassation procedure and divergent legal interpretations
sources.findings: Read Actu-Juridique’s substantive legal analysis: March 31, 2025 and July 7, 2026 sentences, no provisional execution in the appeal ruling, cassation filings, constitutional questions and disputed suspensive effects. December 16 QPC hearing and early-April 2027 target are reported future plans, not completed rulings. Analysis is not the underlying judgment or an authoritative final eligibility determination.

sources.title: Continuing debate over eligibility and cassation effects, 2 November 2026
sources.findings: Read Public Sénat November 2, 2026 explanation of divergent positions. Rémy Heitz rejects revival of the first judgment; Didier Guérin argues original provisional ineligibility persists. Other cited lawyers also disagree. Public copy preserves the dispute without declaring a new court decision, certain disqualification or conclusively certified eligibility. The five-year initial ban is not represented as the unchanged latest sentence.

sources.title: RN group presidency: Chenu replaces Le Pen, published 28 October 2026
sources.findings: Read Légifrance’s original October 28, 2026 JORF notice, NOR INPA2628758X: Assembly president informed that Sébastien Chenu replaces Le Pen as RN group president. Publication is distinguished from the Assembly’s October 27 record and October 24 political announcement. No claim of resignation from her parliamentary seat.

sources.title: Completed meeting with Ukraine’s ambassador and campaign proposals, 16 November 2026
sources.findings: Read Euronews’s November 16, 2026 completed ambassador-meeting account, attributed partly to an RN communiqué. Meeting with Vadym Omelchenko is retrospective; possible future Zelensky meeting is not completed. Campaign aid-policy proposals are not enacted government decisions. July 2026 illustration caption is not the meeting date, and the source’s financial totals were not independently audited.

sources.title: 2026 group changes: presidency replacement recorded on 27 October
sources.findings: Read Assembly 2026 group-change page: replacement of Le Pen by Chenu under October 27 heading, JORF October 28. November 16/17 dates at the top concern a different member’s group change and must not be attached to the RN presidency. Confirms current deputy/former group-president correction.
